page: Amazon Web Services i8ge.metal-48xl is a bare-metal, storage-optimized server powered by 192 dedicated physical cores of the ARMv9 AWS Graviton Neoverse-V2 architecture running at 2.7 GHz. The system features 1536.0 GB of DDR5 memory, providing 8.0 GB of RAM per core, and does not include a GPU. Storage is a defining characteristic, featuring 120,000 GB of local NVMe SSD capacity. Network connectivity is supported by a 300 Gbps baseline bandwidth.

Benchmark results show top-tier performance in multi-threaded and memory-intensive operations. The server achieves top-tier status in stress-ng multi-core CPU performance, Geekbench multi-core scores, and Passmark database operations, alongside a high Redis SET throughput of 378.59 million operations per second. Memory bandwidth is exceptionally strong, with cached read-only speeds reaching 13,947.51 GB/sec and large-block uncached writes at 258.51 GB/sec. However, single-core performance is moderate, as evidenced by average-tier scores in stress-ng single-core and Geekbench single-core tests. Additionally, LLM text generation is a notable bottleneck, with the small 135M model scoring in the bottom 10% at 28.16 tokens per second.

From a cost-efficiency perspective, the bare-metal architecture offers high resource density by combining massive local NVMe storage with 192 dedicated physical cores, eliminating hypervisor overhead. This profile is highly optimized for large-scale databases, high-throughput static web serving, and intensive data-decompression tasks. It is less suited for workloads reliant on high single-threaded performance or real-time LLM text generation.
